question: Does a smaller pure-GAD timestep recover strict convergence on PaiNN-native saddles where dt=0.005 fails?
hypothesis: If the PaiNN result is a numerical-stability artifact, one or more dt values in [0.00025, 0.002] will improve strict stationary recovery without displacement caps, descent gating, or smoothing.
design: Five array tasks, one dt each, on the two IRC-accepted PaiNN saddles at 50/100 pm and three fixed matched seeds. Pure projected GAD only, 300 steps, no cap/collision guard/descent gate/blending/multimode.
decision_rule: Use the best prespecified dt for a later paired GAD/Sella confirmation only if it improves across both candidates/noise levels; report all five dt values and do not select on a single trajectory.

resources.allocation: five concurrent A100 3g.20gb MIG slices, 4 CPU cores and 20G each, 60 minutes

result: Pure GAD had 0/12 strict successes at every prespecified dt: 0.00025, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.005 eV-independent integration units.
next_action: Do not attribute the PaiNN negative result to dt within this tested range; any further change is an algorithmic variant, not pure-GAD retuning.
